study: Gorard, Siddiqui & See 2015, Philosophy for Children (P4C/SAPERE), EEF
delivery_evidence: Teachers trained by SAPERE-accredited trainers in two days of (Level 1) face-to-face training plus additional days of in-school support (Teacher training section, 'two days of training... in-school support... using standardised SAPERE methods').
test_alignment_evidence: Outcomes are broad independent standardized assessments: KS2 reading/writing-GPS/maths national tests (National Pupil Database) and CAT4 cognitive ability test; not tailored to P4C (Tables 5-7, 11; p.20-21).
curriculum_evidence: P4C is described as 'an approach to teaching' / 'a practice of dialogic teaching' applied across the curriculum with 'no complete syllabus or unyielding methodology'; SAPERE supplies recommended stimulus materials/resources but no fixed adopted curriculum (Intervention description). [Judgment call: stimulus materials exist, but report frames it as pedagogy, not a curriculum package.]
outcome_timing_evidence: Included KS2 effect sizes measured KS2 summer 2014 at the end of the trial; CAT4 at the Jan-Feb 2014 post-test—all end-of-intervention, same school period (Tables 5-7, 11).
